questions.q: Why isn't a catalog-view query like sys.database_permissions enough to answer "who actually ran this UPDATE last Tuesday"?
options: It only shows what permissions currently exist, not a historical record of events that occurred
sys.database_permissions doesn't exist in SQL Server
It only works for SELECT statements, never for UPDATE
It requires sysadmin privileges to even run
questions.explain: Catalog views are a point-in-time snapshot of permissions, not an event log — you need SQL Server Audit to record actual actions over time.

questions.q: What does the state_desc column returned by sys.database_permissions indicate?
options: Whether the permission is GRANT, DENY, or GRANT_WITH_GRANT_OPTION
Whether the database is online or offline
The physical state of the underlying table's data file
Whether the login is currently connected
questions.explain: state_desc reports the type of explicit permission statement recorded — GRANT, DENY, or GRANT_WITH_GRANT_OPTION.

questions.q: What is the relationship between a Server Audit and an Audit Specification in SQL Server Audit?
options: The Server Audit defines where events are written; the Audit Specification defines which events get captured
They are two names for the exact same object
The Audit Specification defines where events are written; the Server Audit defines which events are captured
A Server Audit alone, with no specification, is sufficient to capture events
questions.explain: You need both objects — the audit sets the destination, the specification defines the events to capture. An audit alone records nothing.

Creates a new SQL Server Audit object
Deletes old audit files older than a specified date
Grants permissions based on a stored audit policy
questions.explain: fn_get_audit_file is a table-valued function that parses the binary .sqlaudit files into rows you can query with T-SQL.

questions.q: In this lesson's CREATE DATABASE AUDIT SPECIFICATION example, which actions are being captured on dbo.Employee?
options: SELECT and UPDATE, by the public role
Only DELETE operations
Only login attempts, not data access
INSERT and DELETE, by db_owner only
questions.explain: The specification's ADD clause lists SELECT, UPDATE ON dbo.Employee BY public as the events to capture.
